headline: LLM agents gate omics analysis on assumption and calibration checks before execution
label: Computational Biology Workflow Tools
summary: LLM-driven biomedical workflows are now evaluated on whether their outputs satisfy validity conditions, not only on task accuracy.
synthesis: The dominant thread is a validity condition placed inside the step that produces a result, rather than a new core algorithm. DE-Rigor-Agent screens six bulk RNA-seq differential expression methods for assumption compatibility before execution. statLens pairs LLMs, code, and human review for omics statistical analysis and reports 92.5-95.0% accuracy in its evaluation. The ECS framework calibrates LLM line-of-therapy adjudication through human-in-the-loop selection, reporting 5% residual error with 44.6% of cases reviewed in myeloma simulations. The orchestrator comparison addresses a different axis: local Gemma 4 matches larger models on single-turn tasks but lags on multi-turn tasks. These items differ in domain and data type, and only DE-Rigor-Agent directly gates method choice on assumptions. What is new is placement: the check constrains which outputs a workflow can produce.
